In CSS stacking order, elements are painted according to their z-index, where higher z-index values paint later and appear on top of lower ones. Here, `root>middle` has a z-index of 3, which is higher than `root>front` (z-index 2) and `root>back` (z-index 1). Since the point (120, 120) falls within the bounds of `root>middle` and it has the highest z-index with an opaque background, it completely covers the other boxes at that location.

ANSWER: root>middle
